# `Q-13-4` — Body link references missing document

> A link in document body content points at a project file
> that is not in the render index.

## What this means

When you write `[See report](report.qmd)` in a Quarto document,
the renderer rewrites the link so the rendered page links to
`report.html` (the output filename) instead of the source. The
rewrite requires the target to be in the project index — Quarto
has to know the target will exist. This error fires when the
target name does not appear in the index. The link still
renders but with the original `.qmd` path, which the published
site will treat as broken.

This is the warning you will see most often if you are writing
cross-references to pages that have not been authored yet.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A typo in the link target.**
- **A link to a page that is planned but not yet created** —
  this happens during iterative authoring.
- **A link to a deleted page** whose references were not
  cleaned up.
- **An underscore-prefixed file** linked from a non-excluded
  one — the target is intentionally not in the render set.

## How to fix

Make sure the target exists in the project and is in the render
set. If you are linking to a page that does not exist yet,
either create a stub for it now or accept the warning until the
page lands.
